I never said not to impeach Kegsbreath. I said to wait until January and the next. We have a much better chance of succeeding then. Is it likely to end in a conviction? No, but the chances will be better than the near-zero chance now. Plus, it forces the remaining Repugnicans to defend his actions to the people, something they might have to pay for in following elections. It’s solid strategy to wait. Why waste the vote and the political capital on a definite lose-lose situation that’s almost guaranteed to fail? It’s not the same as election, either, because the people decide the elections, not congressional Repugnicans. By the standard you’re using, why not put forward a medicare for all bill right now? Simple, because it’s an almost guaranteed loss and waiting gives it a better chance to at least be considered seriously. We have to pick our battles carefully. I want Kegsbreath in prison just as much as you do, but I’m willing to wait for the best opportunity, also letting him fuck up even more and giving the remaining Repugnicans more reasons to turn on him, especially if we pin the Blue Tsunami on election day partially on his actions in the meantime. Start calling Repug senators now and loudly blame him for Repug losses this year.
